guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the every-other-combat Power card reward option is entirely missing, and it is the game's ONLY implementation of the EARLY TryModifyCardRewardOptions pass
guards.issue: MECHANISM: LastingCandy.cs:114-135 takes `creationOptions.GetPossibleCards(player)`, keeps the Power-type cards not already offered (falling back to all Power cards if that set is empty), builds a fresh CardCreationOptions with source Other and flags NoModifyHooks | NoCardPoolModifications, runs `CardFactory.CreateForReward(Owner, 1, options2)` and APPENDS the result to the options list. lasting_candy.py implements nothing. PREMISE CHECK (PROMPT.md bug class 12): the docstring says 'a card-reward modifier that runs between combats, so this is a no-op stub' -- false. `Relic.modify_card_reward_options` exists (relics/base.py:172-176) and rewards.py:299-301 dispatches it over run.relics inside create_reward_cards; the shared sweep-stub-premises already reports this pipeline as live. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b08.py b08-candy): Lasting Candy is Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag (b08-pool), and a MONSTER card reward on the second combat of a run comes out as the same three cards ['battle_trance', 'twin_strike', 'expect_a_fight'] with and without the relic, where the game adds a fourth, always-Power option. The same probe's b08-lavalamp run shows relic/silver_crucible mutating reward options through that very hook today, so the sim demonstrably can do this. SECOND OBSERVABLE: the added card costs a rarity roll, an item pick and an upgrade roll on the per-player Rewards stream (CardFactory.cs:214-241 and RollForUpgrade at CardFactory.cs, reached because options2 carries no NoUpgradeRoll flag), none of which the sim consumes -- so every later Rewards draw in the run is shifted for the conformance harness. Rule 7: relics/base.py, rewards.py, relics/silver_crucible.py and src/Core/Factories/CardFactory.cs are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): LastingCandy is the SEVENTEENTH member of the `IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest` (TotalFloor < 41) cluster, not a separate 'unlock gate' unit -- correcting .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep B
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: pool eligibility is modelled now. `Relic.is_allowed(run)` exists on the sim's base (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:198, default True) and this relic overrides it with `is_before_act3_treasure_chest(run)` (sts2_rl/relics/lasting_candy.py:16), the `TotalFloor < 41` predicate of RelicModel.IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest (RelicModel.cs:452-456). RunState._drop_disallowed_from_grab_bag (sts2_rl/run.py:769) applies it before EVERY pull and REMOVES the rejects from the bag -- pull_relic_from_front (run.py:731), pull_relic_from_back (run.py:752) and the Shop-rarity bag (run.py:783) are the only three pull paths -- mirroring RelicGrabBag.RemoveDisallowedRelicsFromDeques (RelicGrabBag.cs:218-270), and `Relic.is_allowed_at_neow` now DELEGATES to is_allowed (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:211-222 = RelicModel.cs:443-446) so the Neow pools (sts2_rl/events/neow.py:72) cannot read a stale flag. Verified by execution against today's code: every one of the 17 cluster members returns is_allowed False at total_floor 60 and True at floor 0. WAS: the sim's Relic base declared no is_allowed member at all and populate_relic_grab_bags shuffled the pool once at run init with no per-pull filter, so the relic stayed pullable for the whole run and a late pull also shifted every subsequent pull.

guards.what: G3 (DORMANT): the FIRST clause -- `runState.Players.Any(p => p.Character is Ironclad && p.UnlockState.NumberOfRuns == 0)` vetoes the relic on a profile's very first Ironclad run
guards.issue: MECHANISM: LastingCandy.cs:82-96. The sim has no profile/unlock model at all -- `grep -rn 'UnlockState\|NumberOfRuns' sts2_rl/` returns nothing and RunState has no notion of how many runs the profile has played -- so the sim behaves as a veteran profile always. RECORDED AS A DORMANT GAP, NOT A WAIVER, per binding rule 1: 'the sim has no such system' is explicitly a dormant gap, and unlocks are not one of the contract's four waiver categories (multiplayer, presentation, ascension, other characters). This is the answer sweep B left open ('likely a waiver, but this batch must say so with a reason') -- the reason it is not a waiver is rule 1, and the reason it is dormant rather than live is that the concrete unported thing is a per-profile UnlockState with NumberOfRuns; the conformance seeds all come from a profile with many completed runs, so the clause evaluates false there and the sim's behaviour coincides. It also cannot be the whole story about this relic's IsAllowed -- see G2. The Ironclad-character half of the predicate is inside the shared contract's Ironclad-only scope and needs no waiver.

guards.what: G4 (DORMANT): the sim's single `modify_card_reward_options` collapses C#'s EARLY and LATE card-reward passes, and Lasting Candy is the only early implementer
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions' TWO complete passes are modelled. `Relic` declares `modify_card_reward_options` (the plain pass) and `modify_card_reward_options_late` as SEPARATE members (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:241-251), and rewards.create_reward_cards runs every relic's plain hook and THEN every relic's Late hook (sts2_rl/rewards.py:304-315), which is Hook.cs:1444-1466. A Late implementer is therefore guaranteed to see everything the plain pass added, whatever order the relics were picked up in. WAS: one flat `for relic in list(run.relics)` loop, so the phase guarantee was registration-order luck.
